speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It means that the majority of FDW borrowers have worked in Singapore for some time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It is a combination of supply and demand side factors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: First, it was observed that some licensed moneylenders (LMLs) have been targeting the FDWs through shopfront advertisements and readily extending loans to them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Second, some FDWs have been recommending loans to their fellow FDWs by word-of-mouth, WhatsApp or Facebook.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Third, there are some FDWs acting as guarantors for fellow FDWs to obtain loans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: LMLs are also prohibited from displaying advertisements targeted at FDWs and from accepting foreigners as loan guarantors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM and MinLaw are continuing to monitor the situation very closely.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We are working closely with employers, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and employment agencies to educate FDWs on prudent financial management and the risks and implications of borrowing money.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could I ask, not the top three reasons of how they are borrowing but the top three reasons of why they are borrowing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think there are some reports that say that they are borrowing because of family emergencies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am just wondering how effective our new measures will be.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If it is for family emergencies and we block them from LMLs, will we not then push them to the unlicensed moneylenders that will put them in a more difficult position, the FDWs and the employers as well?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That is why, if we can study the reasons why they are borrowing, then we can address the root of the problem and then come up with policies to address it.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At this juncture, let me share some numbers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We have been monitoring the numbers since we rolled out the measures announced in October 2018.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, the spike has been from 2017 to first half of this year, which really warrants the two rounds of measures.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, there is an option for FDWs to borrow, especially those with genuine needs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And we did the study on not just the supply side consideration but also on the demand side.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Some FDWs borrow because they need to send money back for their children's education, to pay for urgent medical bills, or to renovate or build houses and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If Members think about the numbers that I talked about, actually, in 2016, it was quite stable, at 1,500.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But it spiked seven times to 12,000 in 2017 and then 2018.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The two Ministries studied it and we think that increased financial hardship does not appear to be a reason for the surge in the FDW borrowing.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Nonetheless, we encourage our FDWs to maintain open communications with their employers to talk about their financial needs and also to plan their finances for rainy days.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And we will continue to monitor the situation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: FDWs who need help, other than speaking to employers, we encourage them to also come forward to MOM and the NGOs, including the Centre for Domestic Employees or even the Foreign Domestic Worker Association.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Going back to Mr Louis Ng's question on why FDWs borrow, I mentioned that there are some FDWs with genuine needs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Our study also found that some FDWs are recommending their fellow FDWs to get loans and even going to the extent of being a guarantor for them to get the loan.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: When we did a survey amongst the FDWs who were standing there queuing up to borrow money, some of them did share that they were borrowing money to buy clothes, mobile phones or handbags.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, I think it is a combination of needs and wants.
